title: Describing and comparing
goal: Describe people, places and clothes, and compare two things.

notes.p: Put {{好|hou2}} in front of a describing word. It means "very", but Cantonese uses it even where English says nothing, and no {{係|hai6}} is needed: {{佢好高|keoi5 hou2 gou1}} = he's tall. Two kinds of "short": {{矮|ai2}} for height, {{短|dyun2}} for length. Two kinds of "old": {{舊|gau6}} for things, {{老|lou5}} for people. Tone trap: {{舊|gau6}} (old) is low and flat; {{九|gau2}} (nine) rises.

A {{比|bei2}} B + describing word = A is more … than B. Drop {{好|hou2}} here: say {{佢比我高|keoi5 bei2 ngo5 gou1}}, never {{佢比我好高|keoi5 bei2 ngo5 hou2 gou1}}. For "much more", add {{好多|hou2 do1}} at the end. Add {{啲|di1}} to a describing word for "a bit more", and to ask which one: {{邊個貴啲呀？|bin1 go3 gwai3 di1 aa3}}. You will also hear {{佢高過我|keoi5 gou1 gwo3 ngo5}}, which means the same.
ex: keoi5 bei2 ngo5 gou1 hou2 do1
ni1 go3 bei2 go2 go3 gwai3
This one is more expensive than that one.
jau5 mou5 daai6 di1 ge3 aa3
Do you have a bigger one?

notes.p: {{最|zeoi3}} before a describing word = the most. A {{同|tung4}} B {{一樣|jat1 joeng6}} + describing word = A is as … as B. A {{冇|mou5}} B {{咁|gam3}} + describing word = A isn't as … as B. Here {{咁|gam3}} has a mid level tone.
ex: ngo5 dei6 loeng5 go3 jat1 joeng6 gou1
ngo5 tung4 keoi5 jat1 joeng6 gou1
zi1 gaa1 go1 mou5 hoeng1 gong2 gam3 jit6
Chicago isn't as hot as Hong Kong.

notes.p: Colours end in {{色|sik1}}: {{紅色|hung4 sik1}}, {{藍色|laam4 sik1}}. Two verbs for "wear": {{着|zoek3}} for clothes and shoes, {{戴|daai3}} for things you put on, like a hat, glasses or a watch. Each kind of thing has its measure word: {{件|gin6}} for tops and jackets, {{條|tiu4}} for trousers, {{對|deoi3}} for a pair of shoes, {{間|gaan1}} for shops and restaurants. Changed tones: {{帽|mou2}} (hat) and {{眼鏡|ngaan5 geng2}} (glasses) rise at the end.

notes.h: Seems like, a lot, a little
notes.p: {{好似|hou2 ci5}} + a description = "seems"; {{好似|hou2 ci5}} + a person = "looks like". For amounts: {{好多|hou2 do1}} = a lot, {{少少|siu2 siu2}} = a little. Listen for {{似|ci5}}: it rises from low, so {{好似好攰|hou2 ci5 hou2 gui6}} (seems tired) sounds different from {{好攰|hou2 gui6}} (very tired).
ex: keoi5 hou2 ci5 keoi5 maa4 maa1
There are lots of people here.

vocab.note: For people and buildings. For length use {{短|dyun2}}.
Low and flat. Don't confuse with {{九|gau2}} (nine).
For clothes: looks nice. For a film or show: good.
{{好多人|hou2 do1 jan4}} = lots of people, crowded.

{{邊個|bin1 go3}} = who, or which one.

items.en: He's taller than me.
items.why: A {{比|bei2}} B + describing word = A is more … than B.

items.en: This top is the most expensive.
items.why: {{最|zeoi3}} before a describing word = the most.

q: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 jat1 ___ hak1 sik1 saam1
items.en: I want to buy a black top.
items.why: Tops are counted with {{件|gin6}}.

items.en: I want to buy a pair of trousers.
items.why: Trousers are counted with {{條|tiu4}}, the measure word for long things. English says "a pair", but Cantonese doesn't use {{對|deoi3}} here.

items.en: I bought a pair of shoes.
items.why: {{對|deoi3}} = a pair, used for shoes.

items.en: She wears glasses.
items.why: Glasses, hats and watches take {{戴|daai3}}. {{着|zoek3}} is for clothes and shoes.

q: ngo5 gam1 jat6 ___ hung4 sik1 saam1
items.en: I'm wearing a red top today.
items.why: Clothes take {{着|zoek3}}.

q: ni1 go3 mou5 go2 go3 ___ gwai3
items.en: This one isn't as expensive as that one.
items.why: A {{冇|mou5}} B {{咁|gam3}} + describing word = A isn't as … as B.

items.en: We're the same height.
items.why: {{一樣|jat1 joeng6}} + describing word = equally, the same.

items.en: He looks like his dad.
items.why: {{好似|hou2 ci5}} + a person = looks like. {{一樣|jat1 joeng6}} would need {{同|tung4}} and comes at the end.

items.en: Do you have a bigger one?
items.why: {{啲|di1}} after a describing word = a bit more: {{大啲|daai6 di1}} = bigger.

q: nei5 zung1 ji3 ___ ngaan4 sik1 aa3
items.en: What colour do you like?
items.why: {{咩|me1}} = what, and it goes right before the noun.

q: taai3 sai3 ___, jau5 mou5 daai6 di1 ge3 aa3
items.en: It's too small. Do you have a bigger one?
items.why: {{太|taai3}} … {{喇|laa3}} = too … A final {{咩|me1}} would turn it into a surprised question.

items.en: Hong Kong is crowded.
items.why: {{好多人|hou2 do1 jan4}} = lots of people, crowded.

q: 呢對鞋好___喇，我想買對新嘅
ni1 deoi3 haai4 hou2 ___ laa3, ngo5 soeng2 maai5 deoi3 san1 ge3
items.en: These shoes are really old now; I want to buy a new pair.
items.why: Things are {{舊|gau6}}; people are {{老|lou5}}.

q: zi1 gaa1 go1 ___ hoeng1 gong2 gam3 jit6
items.en: Chicago isn't as hot as Hong Kong.
items.why: "Not as … as" uses {{冇|mou5}}, not {{唔|m4}}: A {{冇|mou5}} B {{咁|gam3}} + describing word.

items.q: In a clothes shop, the top you tried is too small. You ask:
opts: jau5 mou5 daai6 di1 ge3 aa3
jau5 mou5 sai3 di1 ge3 aa3
ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 sai3 ge3
items.why: {{大啲|daai6 di1}} = a bit bigger.

items.q: Your friend tries on a jacket and it looks great on her. You say:
items.why: {{好襯你|hou2 can3 nei5}} = it suits you.

items.q: You like a pair of shoes in a shop and want to try them on. You ask:
opts: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 si3 haa5 aa3
ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 do1 ci3 aa3
ngo5 m4 jiu3 ni1 deoi3 haai4
items.why: {{試吓|si3 haa5}} = try (it) out.

items.q: Someone asks your favourite colour. It's blue. You say:
opts: ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 laam4 sik1
ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3 hung4 sik1
ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 laam4 sik1
items.why: {{我最鍾意|ngo5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3}} = I like … best; {{藍色|laam4 sik1}} = blue.

items.q: Your friend Wing is taller than you. You tell someone:
items.why: The taller person comes first: {{佢比我高|keoi5 bei2 ngo5 gou1}}.

items.q: You're in a busy restaurant and can hardly hear your friend. You say:
items.why: {{嘈|cou4}} = noisy; {{靜|zing6}} = quiet.

items.q: A friend shows you a photo of her daughter, who looks just like her. You say:
opts: keoi5 hai6 bin1 go3 lai4 gaa3
items.why: {{好似|hou2 ci5}} + a person = looks like.

items.q: You hold up two tops and notice they are exactly the same. You say:
items.why: Tops take {{件|gin6}}; {{一樣|jat1 joeng6}} = the same, {{唔同|m4 tung4}} = different.

This one is the cheapest.
I like blue best.

roleplay.title: Shopping for clothes in Mong Kok
roleplay.setup: You're in a small clothes shop in Mong Kok. Find a top you like, ask about colours and sizes, try it on, and compare prices before you buy.
roleplay.persona: You are a friendly shop assistant in a small clothes shop in Mong Kok. You have tops in black, white, blue and red. The red top is two hundred and eighty dollars, the blue one is two hundred dollars. Bigger and smaller sizes are available. Help the learner choose, let them try things on, and compliment them when something suits them. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1 to 9 (measure words 件 and 條, 大啲 / 細啲, 比, 最, 冇咁, 試吓, 好襯你).
opening: 歡迎光臨！想睇吓啲咩呀？
fun1 jing4 gwong1 lam4! soeng2 tai2 haa5 di1 me1 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: Welcome! What would you like to look at?
goals: Ask for a top in a colour you like
Ask for a bigger or smaller size
Compare two prices and choose one

roleplay.title: Hong Kong versus Chicago
roleplay.setup: Ka-yan, a new friend in Hong Kong, has never been to Chicago. Describe your city and compare it with Hong Kong.
roleplay.persona: You are Ka-yan, a friendly young Hong Konger who has never been to Chicago. Ask the learner what Chicago is like: is it big, is it crowded, is it hotter or colder than Hong Kong, is it convenient to get around, which city they like best. React naturally and share your own view of Hong Kong. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese in short sentences, using mostly words from levels 1 to 9, with comparisons using 比, 最, 冇咁 and 一樣.
opening: 芝加哥係點㗎？大唔大呀？
zi1 gaa1 go1 hai6 dim2 gaa3? daai6 m4 daai6 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: What's Chicago like? Is it big?
goals: Say whether Chicago is bigger or smaller than Hong Kong
Compare the weather in the two cities
Describe a place you like with two describing words
Say which city you like best
